internationalAid.note: International applicants may be considered for academic merit and athletic scholarships, but Campbell requires proof that the full first-year cost can be funded independently of a potential athletic award. The reviewed official pages do not promise international need-based aid.

sources.label: Official college page

scholarships.note: Campbell publishes main-campus undergraduate merit programs including Presidential, Scott-Ellis, CU Promise, Campbell Grant, and Faith Grant. International applicants must submit official SAT or ACT results for scholarship consideration even though general admission is test-optional.

sources.label: Official college page

internationalAdmission.note: International applicants submit Campbell's application, certified English translations of school records and national exams, English proof, and certified financial-support documents dated within six months. The page offers a Fall 2027 application route.

sources.label: Official college page

applicationPlansAndDeadlines.note: Campbell uses rolling admission rather than ED, EA, or REA. It accepts completed undergraduate applications until the semester begins, while advising applicants not to wait that late. The international page currently accepts Fall 2027 applications.

sources.label: Official college page

applicationRequirements.note: Required international materials include the admission application, official or certified translated secondary-school records, national examination results and diplomas, English proof, and certified proof of first-year financial support. Passport and U.S. status documents apply when relevant.

sources.label: Official college page

testingPolicy.note: Campbell is test-optional for admission and potential merit review generally, but its international instructions require official SAT or ACT for international scholarship consideration. Submitted scores can also affect placement.

sources.label: Official college page

englishProficiency.note: Campbell accepts TOEFL, IELTS, SAT, or ACT as English proof and publishes IELTS 5.5 as a minimum. The reviewed undergraduate page does not publish a TOEFL, SAT, or ACT English minimum, so applicants should confirm those routes directly.

internationalAid.note: International applicants are considered for partial-tuition scholarships based on academic and extracurricular achievement and financial need. Part-time campus employment may also be available, but the colleges do not promise a full-cost award.

sources.label: Official college page

scholarships.note: International applicants are automatically considered for an International Student Scholarship when they apply and submit the International Student Financial Aid Application. The admission decision includes the academic scholarship amount.

sources.label: Official college page

internationalAdmission.note: International applicants submit the admission application, official secondary and any post-secondary records, English evidence when required, and the International Student Financial Aid Application. Admitted students add Certification of Finances with bank or income evidence.

sources.label: Official college page

applicationPlansAndDeadlines.note: The current catalog lists nonbinding Early Action I on November 1, Early Action II on December 1, then rolling admission. International preferred dates are April 1 for fall and November 15 for spring. The page does not label them as Fall 2027 dates, so they are planning references.

sources.label: Official college page

applicationRequirements.note: A complete international file includes the admission application, official high-school transcript and any college-credit transcripts, English assessment if required, and the International Student Financial Aid Application. An optional writing sample and recommendations can strengthen the file.

sources.label: Official college page

testingPolicy.note: The College of Saint Benedict and Saint John's University are test-optional. SAT or ACT is added to the file only when the applicant chooses to submit it.

sources.label: Official college page

englishProficiency.note: TOEFL, IELTS, Duolingo, PTE Academic, or another approved English assessment is required when English was not the primary language of instruction throughout secondary school. The reviewed current page does not publish university-wide minimum scores.

internationalAid.note: CSU Pueblo offers a defined international merit award but does not publish a promise to meet international financial need. F-1 students must submit financial evidence covering the full remaining cost before visa documents can be issued.

sources.label: Official college page

scholarships.note: The International Merit Scholarship is $8,000 per academic year for new F-1 students with at least a 3.0 incoming GPA who attend international orientation and enroll full time. It is renewable for up to four freshman years, cannot be combined with other institutional non-athletic aid, and uses June 1 for fall enrollment.

sources.label: Official college page

internationalAdmission.note: International first-year applicants need at least a 2.3 weighted high-school GPA, CSU Pueblo's application, a passport, English evidence, financial support, and an approved course-by-course credential evaluation. The university does not publish a current international admit rate.

sources.label: Official college page

applicationPlansAndDeadlines.note: CSU Pueblo uses rolling admission after its preferred dates. The current international page lists June 1 for fall, November 1 for spring, and March 1 for summer, but does not label the dates specifically for Fall 2027; June 1 is therefore a planning reference and is also the published international-merit enrollment deadline.

sources.label: Official college page

applicationRequirements.note: International first-year applicants submit CSU Pueblo's online application, a $30 fee, official secondary records through an approved credential evaluator, English evidence, passport copy, and financial statement. Final secondary results are required after admission when the applicant was still completing school.

sources.label: Official college page

testingPolicy.note: CSU Pueblo is test-optional for undergraduate admission. SAT or ACT can add context, support math placement, or satisfy a scholarship metric, but is not required; international applicants still need an approved English-proficiency route.

sources.label: Official college page

englishProficiency.note: General undergraduate minimums are TOEFL iBT 61 on the former scale or 3.5 on the scale used after January 21, 2026, IELTS Academic 5.5, or Duolingo 95. Nursing requires TOEFL 79–80 or 4.0, IELTS 6.0, or Duolingo 110. Listed English-speaking countries and qualifying U.S. study can provide an exemption.

sources.label: Official college page

internationalAid.note: Hunter does not provide federal or New York State financial aid to students who do not meet eligible-citizen rules. International students should plan to finance tuition and living costs and may research outside awards or competitive Hunter honors scholarships; no international full-need commitment is published.

sources.label: Official college page

scholarships.note: Hunter's Freshman Honors Scholar programs include significant merit scholarships, advising and priority registration. The latest posted cycle used December 15 for priority and February 15 for general consideration, with a separate supplement after the CUNY admission application; Fall 2027 dates and award amounts are not yet published.

sources.label: Official college page

internationalAdmission.note: Applicants educated outside the United States submit complete official secondary records and certified translations either through CUNY or Hunter's recommended evaluation route. Temporary-visa applicants educated in a non-English environment submit an approved English test. Hunter does not publish a current international admit rate.

sources.label: Official college page

applicationPlansAndDeadlines.note: Hunter's current page lists December 1 for the international fall application and December 15 for supporting documents, followed by rolling notification from January through July. The page is not labeled for Fall 2027, so these dates are planning references; completed general applications may be reviewed later if space remains.

sources.label: Official college page

applicationRequirements.note: Freshmen use the CUNY Application, which can include up to six CUNY colleges, and pay a $65 fee. Hunter reviews the secondary transcript, academic performance and rigor, an essay, leadership and intellectual engagement; recommendations are optional. International records and official English scores are added when applicable.

sources.label: Official college page

testingPolicy.note: Hunter's page says it was test-optional only through Spring 2027. A Fall 2027 SAT/ACT policy has not yet been posted, so applicants should not assume the previous temporary policy continues.

sources.label: Official college page

englishProficiency.note: For temporary-visa applicants educated in a non-English environment, Hunter's published undergraduate comparison scores are TOEFL iBT 61 or paper 500, IELTS Academic 6.0, PTE Academic 53, or Duolingo 85. Official results must be sent by the testing agency; these scores support admission and do not replace any later CUNY placement requirement.

sources.label: Official college page

internationalAid.note: International students complete the Emmanuel University Application for Aid for institutional-scholarship consideration. They are not directed to FAFSA-based federal or Georgia aid and must show recent financial evidence covering the 2026–27 remaining annual cost before Emmanuel issues Form I-20.

sources.label: Official college page

scholarships.note: The International Student Scholarship can award up to $15,000 per year to nominated students from an evangelical Christian background who fit Emmanuel's Christ-centered community; it does not stack with an athletic scholarship and nominations are due July 15. The current aid page also lists GPA-based academic merit awards up to $6,000, but applicants should confirm which single institutional award applies.

sources.label: Official college page

internationalAdmission.note: International applicants submit Emmanuel's application, passport copy, recent financial-support statement, English evidence, and course-by-course evaluations of all secondary and college records through a listed service. The university does not publish a current international admit rate.

sources.label: Official college page

applicationPlansAndDeadlines.note: Emmanuel's current international page lists June 30 as the fall priority application date and November 30 for spring. The dates are not labeled specifically for Fall 2027, so June 30 is a planning reference; the separate International Student Scholarship nomination date is July 15.

sources.label: Official college page

applicationRequirements.note: The international file includes Emmanuel's application, passport, financial-support form with a bank statement no older than 90 days, approved English score when required, and course-by-course evaluations of official high-school and college records showing graduation date and GPA.

sources.label: Official college page

testingPolicy.note: SAT and ACT are optional for freshman admission. International students do not need those exams if they meet the separate English requirement through TOEFL, IELTS, Duolingo, or an accepted primary-language exemption.

sources.label: Official college page

englishProficiency.note: Applicants whose primary language is not English submit TOEFL iBT 79–80, IELTS 6.5, or Duolingo 110. Emmanuel describes these as minimum international entrance scores and may require English support classes if later academic work shows a need.

internationalAid.note: Full-time undergraduate international students may apply for institutional financial aid with CSS Profile. Awards depend on eligibility and available funding; Fairfield does not publish a commitment to meet every international applicant's full demonstrated need.

sources.label: Official college page

scholarships.note: Applicants who meet the published admission deadlines receive priority consideration for merit scholarships as well as need-based aid. The reviewed page does not require a separate general merit application.

sources.label: Official college page

internationalAdmission.note: International first-year applicants use Fairfield's standard Common Application route and provide official academic records, approved English proof or waiver, translations or credential evaluation where required, and financial certification for immigration processing.

sources.label: Official college page

applicationPlansAndDeadlines.note: The 2026–27 official catalog lists nonbinding Early Action on November 1, binding Early Decision I on November 15, and binding Early Decision II plus Regular Decision on January 15. EA notification is by January 15, ED I by December 15, ED II by February 15, and RD by April 1.

sources.label: Official college page

applicationRequirements.note: Fairfield exclusively uses Common Application. The required school submission includes the official secondary-school transcript, School Report, and counselor recommendation; international applicants add English proof and translated or evaluated records where applicable.

sources.label: Official college page

testingPolicy.note: Fairfield is test-optional and reviews applicants holistically whether or not they submit SAT or ACT. Submitted scores can be considered in admission; the current page reports a 1300–1410 SAT and 27–31 ACT middle 50% for admitted students.

sources.label: Official college page

englishProficiency.note: Published undergraduate minimums are TOEFL iBT 80, IELTS 6.5, or Duolingo 105. Fairfield may waive testing when secondary education was completed at a school where English is the primary language of instruction.

sources.label: Official college page

scholarships.note: Every international student receives an academic scholarship, but the current official international and scholarship pages do not publish a Fall 2027 award grid or guaranteed amount. Additional athletic and interest-based scholarships may be considered under their own eligibility rules.

sources.label: Official college page

internationalAdmission.note: International freshmen submit Georgetown College's application, an official secondary transcript, and one approved score from TOEFL, IELTS, Duolingo, SAT, or ACT. sources.label: Official college page

internationalAid.note: International students are not eligible for U.S. federal aid. Georgia State offers limited merit funding, including Campus Atlanta awards that waive 50% or 100% of the out-of-state tuition portion for qualified incoming international students; these are not full-tuition awards.

sources.label: Official college page

scholarships.note: Incoming international students with a recalculated 3.6 or higher college-preparatory GPA may be reviewed for full or partial out-of-state tuition waivers. No separate application is required, November 15 applicants receive priority, and awards depend on available funds.

sources.label: Official college page

internationalAdmission.note: International first-year applicants submit the application and $60 fee, required SAT or ACT scores for Fall 2027, official academic records covering at least the three most recent school years and final examinations, English proof, and later immigration documents after admission.

sources.label: Official college page

applicationPlansAndDeadlines.note: For Fall 2027, the application opens August 1, 2026. Nonbinding Early Action and priority scholarship consideration are due November 15, 2026; the final admission application deadline is May 1, 2027. Final document and score deadlines depend on whether admission has already been issued.

sources.label: Official college page

applicationRequirements.note: First-year applicants to the Atlanta Campus use Common Application and pay a $60 fee. International applicants add official secondary transcripts and graduation or examination certificates, English proof, required SAT or ACT scores, and verified translations or documents sent by the school or examination board.

sources.label: Official college page

testingPolicy.note: Georgia State's Atlanta Campus requires SAT or ACT scores for Fall 2026 admission and later, including Fall 2027. Scores combine with the required high-school curriculum GPA in the University System of Georgia Freshman Index.

sources.label: Official college page

englishProficiency.note: Published routes include SAT Reading 480, ACT English 17, TOEFL iBT 69 on the former scale, IELTS Academic 6.0, and additional approved MET or PTE routes. Duolingo is not accepted under the current university-wide rule.

internationalAid.note: Admitted international students receive an individual notification showing Goshen scholarship and grant eligibility. They must document funds for the remaining tuition, housing, food, books, and insurance; the official page does not promise a full-need award.

sources.label: Official college page

scholarships.note: Every admitted traditional first-year student is automatically considered for an academic scholarship. Higher Achievement awards, including the full-tuition President's Leadership Award, require a separate application and published academic or leadership criteria.

sources.label: Official college page

internationalAdmission.note: International first-year applicants submit Goshen's application, WES or InCred evaluation of secondary records, English proof, and—after admission—a passport copy and Financial Affordability Form with certified funding evidence.

sources.label: Official college page

applicationPlansAndDeadlines.note: The current international page lists May 1 for fall applicants educated outside the United States, June 1 for applicants from U.S. institutions, and October 1 for spring. sources.label: Official college page

applicationRequirements.note: Required international materials are the application, credential evaluation through WES or InCred, English evidence, and later passport and financial documentation. First-year and transfer applicants may also use Common Application.

sources.label: Official college page

testingPolicy.note: Goshen is test-optional for first-year admission. Applicants choose whether SAT or ACT is considered; selected achievement-scholarship routes may use scores as one of several eligibility paths.

sources.label: Official college page

englishProficiency.note: Published minimums are TOEFL iBT 79, IELTS 6.0, or Duolingo 105. Applicants whose primary language is English may instead submit SAT or ACT; the current page does not publish an SAT or ACT minimum for that route.

internationalAid.note: Hampton requires international students to document first-year payment or a sponsor before Form I-20 is issued and does not publish an international full-need commitment. Competitive admission merit scholarships are available to qualifying first-year applicants who submit required SAT or ACT scores.

sources.label: Official college page

scholarships.note: Competitive freshman merit scholarships range from $10,000 to $25,000 per academic year. Applicants need at least a 3.5 unweighted GPA and SAT 1000 or ACT 22, must complete the admission file by the November 15 Early Action date for automatic consideration, and cannot use Hampton's test-optional route. Awards renew for three more years with a 3.0 cumulative GPA.

sources.label: Official college page

internationalAdmission.note: International applicants provide Hampton's application, equivalent secondary credentials with translations and a NACES-aligned evaluation when required, and an approved SAT, ACT, TOEFL, or Duolingo result. Financial documentation is required before Form I-20; Hampton does not publish a current international admit rate.

sources.label: Official college page

applicationPlansAndDeadlines.note: Hampton's current page lists nonbinding Early Action on November 15 with notification by January 15, and a standard March 1 deadline followed by rolling decisions. The page is not labeled specifically for Fall 2027, so these dates are planning references rather than confirmed current-cycle deadlines.

sources.label: Official college page

applicationRequirements.note: Applicants submit Hampton's online application, a $60 nonrefundable fee with no fee waivers, official secondary transcript, one teacher or counselor recommendation, and the required score route. Students attending school outside the United States must submit standardized scores even when some domestic applicants qualify as test-optional.

sources.label: Official college page

testingPolicy.note: Domestic-style applicants with a 3.60 unweighted GPA or top-10-percent rank can choose test-optional review, but students attending schools outside the United States and merit-scholarship candidates must submit SAT or ACT. Hampton superscores SAT sections and uses the highest ACT composite.

sources.label: Official college page

englishProficiency.note: Hampton accepts Duolingo 100 in place of SAT, ACT, or TOEFL for international admission. The 2026–27 catalog also lists paper TOEFL 550, but the current public page does not publish an IELTS minimum or a clear current TOEFL iBT minimum; applicants using those exams should confirm the required score with admission.

internationalAid.note: Hiram offers a limited number of partial-tuition merit scholarships to international first-year and transfer applicants and requires international students to be prepared for the remaining total cost. It does not publish a full-need commitment.

sources.label: Official college page

scholarships.note: For 2026–27, admitted international students received a renewable $15,000 annual Global Scholarship and could also receive a $9,440 Access Grant, with no separate scholarship application. Fall 2027 amounts are not yet published, so these are prior-cycle references.

sources.label: Official college page

internationalAdmission.note: International first-year applicants use Hiram's free International Student Application, submit a NACES evaluation of secondary-school credentials, and provide an approved English score. Canadian and regionally accredited international-school records may be exempt from evaluation.

sources.label: Official college page

applicationPlansAndDeadlines.note: The latest cycle-specific international scholarship page lists June 1, 2026 for Fall 2026 and October 1, 2026 for Spring 2027. A Fall 2027 admission or scholarship deadline and ED, EA, or REA plans are not published.

sources.label: Official college page

applicationRequirements.note: Required materials are the no-fee International Student Application, NACES evaluation of secondary-school transcripts unless an official exemption applies, and English proficiency evidence. Documents may be uploaded in Hiram's portal.

sources.label: Official college page

testingPolicy.note: Hiram's latest accessible official Common Data Set says SAT and ACT are not used in first-year admission decisions. Applicants can still use SAT or ACT to satisfy English proficiency, while nursing and accelerated professional pathways publish separate score requirements.

sources.label: Official college page

englishProficiency.note: Published minimums are TOEFL iBT 79, IELTS 6.0, SAT EBRW 520, ACT English 22, MET 55, PTE 58, SAKAE 10, or Duolingo 105. A-level English B, IB HL English 5, AP English 4, ELS 112, and listed education or citizenship routes can qualify for exemption.

internationalAid.note: Midway offers institutional academic, athletic and talent awards, but does not publish a commitment to meet international financial need. International applicants must contact international admission for an eligibility review and document the remaining first-year funds before Form I-20.

sources.label: Official college page

scholarships.note: Midway publishes academic merit, athletic and talent-based scholarship categories and says merit consideration begins around a 2.5 GPA and ACT 18 or SAT equivalent. It does not publish a current international-specific award grid or guaranteed Fall 2027 amount; the full-tuition Pinkerton Scholarship is explicitly unavailable to international students.

sources.label: Official college page

internationalAdmission.note: International undergraduates submit Midway's application, official credential evaluation, English or native-English testing route, financial guarantee with supporting bank evidence, sponsor letter when applicable, and passport copy. Midway does not publish a current international admit rate.

sources.label: Official college page

applicationPlansAndDeadlines.note: The current academic-catalog admission section lists June 1 for fall international applications and November 1 for spring. It is not labeled specifically for Fall 2027, so June 1 is shown only as a planning reference.

sources.label: Official college page

applicationRequirements.note: Applicants complete Midway's international application, pay a $50 undergraduate international processing and mailing fee, arrange official evaluation of secondary and any college work, submit the required English or SAT/ACT route, provide financial-guarantee evidence and sponsor letter if needed, and upload the passport photo page.

sources.label: Official college page

testingPolicy.note: Non-native English speakers use TOEFL, IELTS, Duolingo or PTE and do not need SAT or ACT solely for admission. Midway says native English speakers submit SAT or ACT. A qualifying U.S. college-level English course can waive the English exam.

sources.label: Official college page

englishProficiency.note: Generally required minimums are TOEFL iBT 61 or paper 500, IELTS 6.0, Duolingo 85, or PTE 44. A grade of C or higher in a U.S. college-level English course can waive the test requirement.

sources.label: Official college page

internationalAid.note: Milligan automatically considers admitted first-year students for academic merit scholarships through either a score-based or test-optional review. It does not publish an international full-need commitment; international students must document support and prepay or arrange the required financial guarantee after admission.

sources.label: Official college page

scholarships.note: For the latest published cycle, automatic academic awards range from $12,000 to $25,000 per year and renew for up to four years. The Jeanes Honors Scholarship awards two full-tuition scholarships, including international candidates, with 3.5 GPA and 29 ACT, 1340 SAT or 90 CLT plus a separate application and interview; Fall 2027 amounts and dates are not yet published.

sources.label: Official college page

internationalAdmission.note: International applicants complete Milligan's standard application, send official secondary records through the required course-by-course evaluation route, demonstrate English or the listed academic-test alternative, and complete financial-support steps after admission. Milligan does not publish a current international admit rate.

sources.label: Official college page

applicationPlansAndDeadlines.note: Milligan uses rolling admission but requires international materials by June 1 for fall and December 1 for spring. These dates are not labeled specifically for Fall 2027, so June 1 is a planning reference; December 1 is also the usual maximum-aid and honors consideration date.

sources.label: Official college page

applicationRequirements.note: Applicants submit Milligan's application with a $30 fee, official secondary records and a course-by-course evaluation including a U.S. 4.0 GPA conversion, approved English or academic-test evidence, and the international questionnaire and financial-support materials needed for Form I-20.

sources.label: Official college page

testingPolicy.note: Milligan allows first-year admission and merit consideration with or without SAT, ACT or CLT. The test-optional route requires at least a 3.25 GPA for automatic merit review and may request a writing sample; international applicants still use an approved English route, while applicants from listed English-speaking countries submit SAT or ACT.

sources.label: Official college page

englishProficiency.note: Published minimums are TOEFL iBT 79 on the former scale or 4.5 after January 21, 2026, IELTS 6.5, Duolingo 110, ELS Level 112, or EIKEN Pre-1/1 for applicants in Japan. Applicants from listed English-speaking countries are directed to SAT or ACT instead.

sources.label: Official college page

internationalAid.note: International undergraduates are not eligible for federal aid but are eligible for Mount institutional merit scholarships. The university does not publish a commitment to meet full international financial need, so students must plan and document the remaining cost.

sources.label: Official college page

scholarships.note: For Fall 2026, automatic first-year merit awards are Trustee $35,000, Presidential $34,000, Provost $33,000, Dean's $30,000 and University $27,000 per year. International undergraduates are eligible for institutional merit awards, but Fall 2027 amounts are not yet published.

sources.label: Official college page

internationalAdmission.note: International undergraduates complete the free international application, submit certified English translations and a course-by-course evaluation of academic records, and provide approved English evidence. Financial documents are completed for immigration processing after admission. The Mount does not publish a current international admit rate.

sources.label: Official college page

applicationPlansAndDeadlines.note: The Mount admits on a rolling basis with nonbinding Early Action I on November 1, Early Action II on December 1, and a February 1 priority financial-aid date. These general dates are not labeled specifically for Fall 2027, so they are planning references.

sources.label: Official college page

applicationRequirements.note: First-year applicants use Mount Application or Common Application, submit official secondary transcripts, and ordinarily pay $25; an official visit can provide a fee waiver. Essay and recommendation are optional. International applicants use the dedicated free application and add translated records, evaluation and English evidence.

sources.label: Official college page

testingPolicy.note: The Mount does not require SAT, ACT or CLT for most admission or merit decisions. International students in a non-English-based secondary curriculum must submit SAT, ACT, TOEFL or IELTS, while the international page also lists several additional English exams.

sources.label: Official college page

englishProficiency.note: Published routes are TOEFL iBT 80, IELTS 6.5, PTE 55, Duolingo 105, Cambridge C1 Advanced, iTEP 4.5, SAT EBRW 530, or ACT English 18. Applicants from qualifying English-based curricula may not need a separate English exam.

internationalAid.note: NYU says first-time first-year students at the New York campus, including international students, can receive need-based NYU scholarship and have 100% of demonstrated need met when they apply by the aid deadline. International applicants seeking aid are need-aware in admission.

sources.label: Official college page

scholarships.note: First-year applicants of any citizenship use CSS Profile for NYU scholarship consideration. NYU offers mainly need-based scholarships and very few purely merit awards. Under NYU Promise, eligible New York-campus first-year students with family income below $100,000 and typical assets have tuition covered.

sources.label: Official college page

internationalAdmission.note: International applicants use NYU's qualification tool to identify required school records and leaving examinations. Applications may use unofficial academic records for review, with official final proof required before enrollment; English testing is required unless an official exemption applies.

sources.label: Official college page

applicationPlansAndDeadlines.note: For Fall 2027, binding Early Decision I is due November 1, 2026, binding Early Decision II is due January 1, 2027, and Regular Decision is due January 5, 2027. Audition, portfolio, and other artistic-review deadlines vary by program and can be later than the university application date.

sources.label: Official college page

applicationRequirements.note: NYU uses Common Application across its three degree-granting campuses. The standard first-year file includes the NYU questions, school report and transcript, one recommendation, STARS academic record, and an $85 fee or approved fee waiver. Selected programs require auditions, portfolios, or other creative materials.

sources.label: Official college page

testingPolicy.note: NYU's current undergraduate qualification tool supports a test-optional application route. Applicants who submit testing can use NYU's flexible-testing options, which may include SAT, ACT, AP, IB, or approved national examinations depending on their curriculum and campus or program.

sources.label: Official college page

englishProficiency.note: English testing is required unless English is the applicant's first language or the applicant has completed three consecutive years in a curriculum where English is the only language of instruction. NYU accepts TOEFL, IELTS Academic, Duolingo, PTE Academic, iTEP, C1 Advanced, and C2 Proficiency; the reviewed university-wide page does not publish minimum scores.

internationalAid.note: NC State states that international applicants are not eligible for financial aid. A limited number of competitive merit scholarships can be pursued after admission through PACK ASSIST, and Fall 2027 visa documentation requires proof of $58,423 in estimated expenses.

sources.label: Official college page

scholarships.note: Admitted international students may apply for a limited number of competitive merit scholarships through PACK ASSIST. The Park Scholarship has separate eligibility rules and is available only to U.S. citizens, permanent residents, or students graduating from a U.S. high school.

sources.label: Official college page

internationalAdmission.note: International first-year applicants use Common Application or Coalition on Scoir, pay a $100 fee with no fee waiver, submit official translated secondary-school records, official English proof, and financial documentation. Applicants choose up to two majors and selected design or music programs require a portfolio and additional essay.

sources.label: Official college page

applicationPlansAndDeadlines.note: The current first-year timeline lists nonbinding Early Action on November 1 with materials due November 15, and Regular Decision on January 15 with materials due February 1. It does not label those dates as Fall 2027, so they are planning references; international decisions are released on a rolling basis after completion.

sources.label: Official college page

applicationRequirements.note: Applicants submit Common Application or Coalition on Scoir, a $100 international fee, official school transcripts and certified English translations, English proof, and financial evidence. Studio-based majors and Music Technology require a ten-piece or program-specific portfolio and an additional essay.

sources.label: Official college page

testingPolicy.note: SAT, ACT, or CLT is optional for international applicants and for applicants with a weighted GPA of at least 2.8. Applicants educated in the U.S. with a weighted GPA from 2.5 to below 2.8 must submit SAT or ACT; scores may be self-reported for review and verified after enrollment.

sources.label: Official college page

englishProficiency.note: Full-admission minimums are TOEFL 80 with each section at least 18 on the former scale or 4.5 with each section at least 4 on the new scale, IELTS 6.5 with sections at least 6.0, Duolingo 110, PTE 58, or successful Level 6 in NC State's Intensive English Program. Lower published scores can qualify for conditional admission.

sources.label: Official college page

internationalAid.note: OCU offers merit and talent scholarships but does not publish an international full-need commitment. International applicants submit financial evidence covering the first-year remaining cost before immigration documents are issued.

sources.label: Official college page

scholarships.note: For 2026–27, automatic merit for first-year Arts and Sciences, Business or Nursing students ranges from $8,000 to $13,000 per year, while Dance, Music and Theatre merit ranges from $3,000 to $6,000; awards renew with a 3.0 GPA. Competitive awards use a December 15 priority date and may cover full cost, but Fall 2027 amounts are not yet published.

sources.label: Official college page

internationalAdmission.note: International freshmen complete OCU's international application, provide official secondary records and national results, meet a 2.5 GPA expectation, submit English evidence, financial-support documents and passport, and complete immigration steps after admission. OCU does not publish a current international admit rate.

sources.label: Official college page

applicationPlansAndDeadlines.note: OCU uses rolling first-year admission throughout the year. Its current scholarship page uses December 15 for priority competitive-scholarship consideration, but the date is not labeled for Fall 2027, so it is a planning reference rather than a confirmed current-cycle deadline.

sources.label: Official college page

applicationRequirements.note: International freshmen use the OCU International Application and pay the $60 online international fee, send official secondary records, English evidence, financial statement and passport. OCU's general first-year application also uses a counselor recommendation; a résumé and extra recommendation strengthen competitive-scholarship consideration.

sources.label: Official college page

testingPolicy.note: OCU is test-optional for SAT and ACT. Applicants without a score receive holistic review based on GPA, curriculum, involvement, service, leadership and recommendations; international applicants still provide an approved English route unless exempt.

sources.label: Official college page

englishProficiency.note: Regular-admission minimums are TOEFL iBT 79, IELTS 6.5 overall with each sub-band at least 6.0, PTE 53, Duolingo 95, ELS Level 112, or a university-approved English institute. Lower TOEFL 60–78, IELTS 6.0 or PTE 48–52 may support provisional admission in selected programs; nursing has higher requirements.

internationalAid.note: Randolph commits at least $14,000 in institutional merit and incentives to every international student, with additional GPA-based amounts. It does not state that it meets full international need; applicants submit one-year financial documentation for the remaining cost.

sources.label: Official college page

scholarships.note: Every international student receives at least $14,000. The WildCat Commitment adds $2,000 for a 3.0 GPA, $3,000 for 3.25, $4,000 for 3.5, or $5,000 for 3.75 or higher, subject to annual cost changes. Randolph also runs a competitive full-tuition Presidential Scholarship, whose next Fall 2027 deadline is not yet published.

sources.label: Official college page

internationalAdmission.note: International applicants use Randolph Application or Common Application and submit official secondary records and leaving certificate, one approved academic or English score, financial-support evidence, and optional recommendations. Randolph does not publish a current international admit rate.

sources.label: Official college page

applicationPlansAndDeadlines.note: Randolph's international page lists March 1 for fall and November 1 for spring. Its latest viewbook also lists nonbinding Early Action on November 15 and Regular Decision March 1. These dates are not labeled specifically for Fall 2027, so they are planning references.

sources.label: Official college page

applicationRequirements.note: Applicants use Randolph Application or Common Application, send official secondary transcript and leaving certificate when applicable, submit one of SAT, ACT, TOEFL, IELTS, PTE or Duolingo, and provide a certified bank statement showing one year of support. Two teacher or counselor recommendations are optional but strongly recommended.

sources.label: Official college page

testingPolicy.note: Randolph is generally test-optional for SAT and ACT, but international applicants submit one approved academic or English exam as part of the international checklist. An English test can satisfy the route without SAT or ACT.

sources.label: Official college page

englishProficiency.note: Published routes are SAT Reading/Writing 500, ACT English/Reading 23, TOEFL iBT 79, IELTS 6.5, Duolingo 100, or PTE Academic 54. Applicants who meet the SAT or ACT English threshold do not need an additional English exam.

sources.label: Official college page

internationalAdmission.note: International applicants follow the same application and portfolio requirements as other applicants, add English proof when required, and provide translated or evaluated academic credentials where applicable.

sources.label: Official college page

applicationPlansAndDeadlines.note: Ringling currently accepts applications on a rolling basis for most majors. Computer Animation has a January 15 application deadline and May 1 confirmation deadline. The page does not label these as Fall 2027 dates, so they are planning references until the cycle is confirmed.

sources.label: Official college page

applicationRequirements.note: Applicants use Common Application, pay a $70 fee or document an approved fee waiver, submit official secondary-school records, a 250–650 word Common App essay, and a digital visual or written portfolio for every major. Recommendations are optional.

sources.label: Official college page

testingPolicy.note: SAT and ACT are not required for admission. Ringling encourages applicants who test to submit scores for academic advising; separate homeschool-document routes may require scores in limited circumstances.

sources.label: Official college page

englishProficiency.note: Published minimums are TOEFL iBT 61, IELTS 6.0, or Duolingo 90. The official catalog also lists SAT Reading and Writing 450 or ACT English 18. Higher scores may allow the college's additional English-support course to be waived after assessment.

sources.label: Official college page

applicationRequirements.note: Applicants submit Ripon Application or Common Application, an unofficial English transcript initially, a counselor or teacher recommendation, one accepted test result, and the Certificate of Finance with bank evidence. sources.label: Official college page

testingPolicy.note: Ripon is test-optional for domestic SAT or ACT review, but every international applicant must submit TOEFL, IELTS, GTEC, Duolingo, SAT or ACT. Applicants can use an English exam instead of SAT or ACT.

englishProficiency.note: Minimums are TOEFL iBT 79 or paper 550, IELTS 6.5, GTEC CBT 1200 or GTEC 1204, Duolingo 110, SAT Critical Reading 590, or ACT English/Writing 24.

sources.label: Official college page

internationalAid.note: International students are not eligible for federal or state aid but can receive Rockhurst merit and talent scholarships. Rockhurst does not publish a commitment to meet full international need, and applicants must prove funding for at least one year before Form I-20.

sources.label: Official college page

scholarships.note: Rockhurst states that international undergraduate merit scholarships range from $14,000 to $28,000, with additional athletics, performing-arts and writing awards in varying amounts. Merit consideration is automatic through admission; the competitive Trustees' Scholarship covers full tuition and normally requires applying before January 1.

sources.label: Official college page

internationalAdmission.note: International freshmen use Rockhurst Online Application or Common Application and submit official secondary records, a counselor recommendation, approved English evidence or waiver documentation, and finances for Form I-20. A credential evaluation may be requested. Rockhurst does not publish a current international admit rate.

sources.label: Official college page

applicationPlansAndDeadlines.note: Rockhurst reviews applications on a rolling basis and gives priority to fall freshman applications received by December 1. The date is not labeled specifically for Fall 2027; January 1 is the latest published Trustees' Scholarship application cutoff, also unconfirmed for Fall 2027.

sources.label: Official college page

applicationRequirements.note: Applicants use Rockhurst Online Application or Common Application and submit secondary transcripts, which can be unofficial for review but must become official before enrollment. International students add a counselor recommendation, official English evidence or waiver, and immigration financial documents.

sources.label: Official college page

testingPolicy.note: All undergraduate programs are test-optional for SAT and ACT, and score omission does not disadvantage admission. Rockhurst superscores when multiple results are submitted; international applicants still meet English proficiency unless a citizenship or full English-curriculum waiver applies.

sources.label: Official college page

englishProficiency.note: Accepted routes are TOEFL iBT 80 or paper 550, TOEFL ITP Plus China 627, IELTS 6.5, PTE 54, Duolingo 110, SAT EBRW 550, ACT English 21, or a qualifying U.S. college English course. Citizenship in a listed English-speaking country or completion of the entire high-school curriculum in English can waive testing.

internationalAid.note: Russell Sage offers institutional merit opportunities to undergraduate applicants, including international students, but does not publish a commitment to meet full international need. International students submit a financial statement and supporting bank documents for the remaining cost before Form I-20.

sources.label: Official college page

scholarships.note: For 2026–27, first-year merit and institutional scholarships range from $21,000 to $26,000 and continue for four years with full-time enrollment and good academic standing. Russell Sage promotes at least $80,000 over four years, but Fall 2027 amounts are not yet published.

sources.label: Official college page

internationalAdmission.note: International applicants use Sage Application or Common Application, submit official transcripts with course-by-course evaluation when the language of instruction is not English, an essay, and English evidence. Financial forms, passport and sponsor documents follow for Form I-20. Russell Sage does not publish a current international admit rate.

sources.label: Official college page

applicationPlansAndDeadlines.note: Russell Sage lists May 1 for international fall application materials and June 1 for Form I-20 eligibility documents. Its catalog also lists nonbinding Early Action I December 1 and Early Action II February 1. These dates are not labeled for Fall 2027, so they are planning references.

sources.label: Official college page

applicationRequirements.note: There is no application fee. Applicants use Sage Application or Common Application, submit official secondary records and required evaluation, a personal essay, and English evidence when instruction was not in English. Immigration financial statement, sponsor support and passport are required after acceptance.

sources.label: Official college page

testingPolicy.note: Russell Sage's international first-year checklist does not require SAT or ACT for admission. Applicants whose language of instruction is not English submit TOEFL or IELTS; an older catalog also lists SAT Reading/Writing as an alternative, but the current public checklist should control.

sources.label: Official college page

englishProficiency.note: The current international page requires TOEFL iBT 85 or IELTS 6.5 when the language of instruction is not English. A course-by-course transcript evaluation is also required in that situation; the catalog's older recommended TOEFL 80 is not used over the current page.

internationalAid.note: Saint John's automatically considers international applicants for an International Student Scholarship after they apply for admission and submit the International Student Financial Aid Application. The college does not publish a commitment to meet full international need; admitted students document enough funding for the remaining cost before Form I-20.

sources.label: Official college page

scholarships.note: International scholarships range up to $38,000 per year and can renew for four years while the student makes satisfactory academic progress. Admission plus the International Student Financial Aid Application provides automatic consideration; student employment may add earnings of up to about $4,000 in a school year.

sources.label: Official college page

internationalAdmission.note: International first-year applicants use the Common Application or CSB+SJU Application, send official secondary and any postsecondary records, provide English evidence when required, submit one core-subject teacher evaluation, and complete the international financial-aid form. Saint John's does not publish a current international admit rate.

sources.label: Official college page

applicationPlansAndDeadlines.note: The current admission timeline lists nonbinding Early Action I November 1, Early Action II December 1, and Regular Decision January 15, with later files reviewed on a rolling basis. The page does not identify these dates specifically as Fall 2027, so they are planning references rather than confirmed Fall 2027 deadlines.

sources.label: Official college page

applicationRequirements.note: There is no application fee. Applicants use Common Application or CSB+SJU Application, provide official academic records, one core-subject teacher evaluation, optional essay, approved English evidence when needed, and the International Student Financial Aid Application. Certification of Finances and bank or income evidence are required after admission for Form I-20.

sources.label: Official college page

testingPolicy.note: SAT and ACT are recommended but not required for international admission. Applicants whose secondary instruction has not been primarily in English submit an approved English test; an academic test does not replace that requirement unless the college confirms an alternative.

sources.label: Official college page

englishProficiency.note: Saint John's accepts TOEFL, IELTS, Duolingo English Test, PTE Academic, or another approved English assessment when secondary instruction was not primarily in English. The current official page does not publish minimum scores, so applicants should confirm the required result directly with international admission.

internationalAid.note: International undergraduates can apply for the JFK International Student Scholarship and may also be considered for institutional scholarship opportunities. Shippensburg does not publish a commitment to meet full international need, and applicants provide financial-support documentation for the remaining cost.

sources.label: Official college page

scholarships.note: The JFK Scholarship/Tuition Reduction Program is available to F-1 undergraduate students and requires the international admission application plus a short program-of-study and contribution statement. The official page confirms awards for 2026–27 and asks Fall 2026 applicants to complete the process before August 1; it does not publish the award amount or Fall 2027 deadline.

sources.label: Official college page

internationalAdmission.note: International undergraduates submit Shippensburg's online application, a course-by-course evaluation of foreign academic work, approved English evidence, and financial-support documents. The university does not publish a current international admit rate.

sources.label: Official college page

applicationPlansAndDeadlines.note: Shippensburg uses rolling admission. Its current international page recommends June 15 for fall applicants living outside the United States and November 1 for spring, but it does not label June 15 as a confirmed Fall 2027 deadline. The date is therefore a planning reference.

sources.label: Official college page

applicationRequirements.note: Applicants complete Shippensburg's international undergraduate application, pay $45, submit a course-by-course evaluation from an approved evaluator, provide official English evidence or a published exemption route, and send financial-support documentation. The general first-year checklist requires the secondary transcript; essay and recommendations are recommended rather than required.

sources.label: Official college page

testingPolicy.note: Shippensburg does not require or review SAT or ACT for general undergraduate admission. Non-native English-speaking international applicants still provide TOEFL, IELTS or Duolingo; international students may also submit SAT or ACT where the international page permits an English-proficiency alternative.

sources.label: Official college page

englishProficiency.note: Published recommended minimums are TOEFL iBT 66 or paper 550, IELTS 6.0, or Duolingo 95. Applicants from a country where English is native or official may use the exemption route, for which the page requires SAT Evidence-Based Reading and Writing 560.

sources.label: Official college page

internationalAid.note: International first-year students are automatically considered for merit scholarships covering up to 63% of tuition. Awards exclude living expenses and fees, require on-campus residence, and renew annually; Saint Mary's does not publish a commitment to meet full international need.

sources.label: Official college page

scholarships.note: The current international freshman grid lists Presidential $30,000, Trustee $29,000, De LaSalle $28,000, Dean's $27,000, and Achievement $25,500 awards based on GPA. Consideration is automatic, awards renew annually, and recipients must live on campus.

sources.label: Official college page

internationalAdmission.note: International undergraduates apply free through Saint Mary's or Common Application, submit an official high-school transcript and approved English evidence, and may need a credential evaluation if the university cannot evaluate the transcript directly. Saint Mary's does not publish a current international admit rate.

sources.label: Official college page

applicationPlansAndDeadlines.note: The current international page says applications are accepted at any time and advises arranging the F-1 visa appointment at least a month before the semester. A more detailed page lists July 1 for fall, but because the current overview says rolling, applicants should use July 1 only as a conservative planning date and confirm Fall 2027 timing.

sources.label: Official college page

applicationRequirements.note: There is no application fee. Applicants use Saint Mary's Application or Common Application, submit official secondary records with a course-by-course evaluation when required, approved English evidence, a 650-word essay, and optional recommendations.

sources.label: Official college page

testingPolicy.note: Saint Mary's is test-optional for SAT and ACT admission and merit scholarships. International applicants who must prove English can use an approved academic or English exam; specific professional programs and non-graded or home-school applicants have separate testing rules.

sources.label: Official college page

englishProficiency.note: Current official pages agree on TOEFL iBT 72 and IELTS 6.0 but conflict on Duolingo, listing 105 on the international overview and 110 or 100 in parts of the detailed page. Until Saint Mary's reconciles the pages, applicants should confirm the Duolingo minimum; the detailed page also lists PTE 51, iTEP 4.0 and several waiver routes.

sources.label: Official college page

internationalAid.note: Stanford meets demonstrated need for admitted international students who request aid when applying. Asking for aid is considered in international admission, and students who say they will not seek aid generally cannot apply for Stanford need-based aid later.

sources.label: Official college page

scholarships.note: Stanford undergraduate institutional scholarships are need-based. No separate application is required for named Stanford scholarship funds; Stanford does not offer general merit scholarships outside limited athletic awards.

sources.label: Official college page

internationalAdmission.note: Stanford publishes overall admission totals but its reviewed official Common Data Set page does not provide international applicant and admit counts needed for a reliable international admit rate.

sources.label: Official college page

applicationPlansAndDeadlines.note: Stanford's current first-year page lists Restrictive Early Action on November 1 and Regular Decision on January 5. Optional arts applicants have earlier application and portfolio dates.

sources.label: Official college page

applicationRequirements.note: The Common Application, $100 fee or waiver, SAT or ACT, School Report and counselor letter, official academic records, midyear transcript, and two academic teacher recommendations are required.

sources.label: Official college page

testingPolicy.note: Stanford requires SAT or ACT, accepts self-reported scores for review, verifies scores after enrollment, and superscores SAT sections and ACT results. The Class of 2029 submitted-score middle 50% was 1520–1570 SAT and 34–36 ACT.

sources.label: Official college page

internationalAid.note: UC Santa Cruz does not offer need-based financial assistance to international students. Applicants must document sufficient funds for nonresident tuition, university charges and living expenses after admission.

sources.label: Official college page

scholarships.note: New international first-year students are considered for the Undergraduate Dean's Award, currently listed at $12,000 to $100,000 total across four years. The UC admission application also serves as the scholarship application; international students should not expect need-based UC aid.

sources.label: Official college page

internationalAdmission.note: International first-year applicants complete the UC application, report all coursework exactly as it appears without converting grades, satisfy UC subject and secondary-completion requirements, and demonstrate English when applicable. They do not send transcripts or extra documents with the application. UCSC does not publish a current international admit rate.

sources.label: Official college page

applicationPlansAndDeadlines.note: For Fall 2027, the UC application filing deadline is November 30, 2026. UCSC does not offer ED, EA, REA or ED2 for first-year applicants; the single UC deadline and later UC notification and enrollment dates apply.

sources.label: Official college page

applicationRequirements.note: Applicants use the University of California application, self-report all international coursework and grades as shown on the original record, complete the UC personal-insight and activity sections, and satisfy subject, secondary-completion and English requirements. Do not send recommendations, transcripts, awards or extra materials unless requested after admission.

sources.label: Official college page

testingPolicy.note: UC campuses do not consider SAT or ACT for admission decisions or scholarships. Submitted scores may only support limited eligibility requirements or placement after enrollment, and English-proficiency evidence remains separate.

sources.label: Official college page

englishProficiency.note: Applicants with fewer than three years of English-medium secondary schooling generally need proof. Current routes include TOEFL new-scale 4.5, IELTS 6.5, Duolingo 115, ACT English Language Arts 24, SAT Writing and Language 31, qualifying AP or IB English results, or an approved UC-transferable composition course.

internationalAid.note: UIC states that international students are not eligible for federal, state, or institutional need-based financial aid. Applicants should plan to cover the full cost unless they receive a separately awarded merit scholarship or outside support.

sources.label: Official college page

scholarships.note: UIC automatically considers first-year applicants for many university scholarships by the November 2, 2026 Fall 2027 priority date, but the current official pages do not identify a named general scholarship with published award terms for F-1 freshmen. Major listed awards such as Chancellor's Fellows require Illinois residency and eligible U.S. status.

sources.label: Official college page

internationalAdmission.note: International first-year applicants follow the Common Application process, submit official secondary records and certified translations where needed, meet English requirements, and provide financial certification. UIC evaluates foreign credentials internally and does not publish a current international admit rate.

sources.label: Official college page

applicationPlansAndDeadlines.note: For Fall 2027, nonbinding Early Action and the first-year scholarship priority deadline are November 2, 2026. Regular Decision is February 1, 2027. Applications and every supporting document must be complete by the applicable date; GPPA and Honors have the same early priority date and additional requirements.

sources.label: Official college page

applicationRequirements.note: First-year applicants use Common Application with UIC questions and essays, pay a $70 fee, and send official high-school transcripts. UIC does not offer international application-fee waivers. SAT or ACT is optional; recommendations and the midyear report are encouraged, while Honors and GPPA require supplemental essays and two recommendations.

sources.label: Official college page

testingPolicy.note: UIC offers separate test-optional and test-inclusive review. Choosing test-optional does not reduce admission, merit-scholarship, Honors, or GPPA eligibility. UIC does not superscore or accept Common App self-reported scores; a score on the transcript, an identifying score report, or an agency report is accepted for test-inclusive review.

sources.label: Official college page

englishProficiency.note: Published minimums are TOEFL iBT 80 on the former scale or 4.5 on the new scale, IELTS 6.5 overall with each section at least 6.0, or PTE 54 with published section minimums. UIC also accepts its Tutorium assessment; qualifying English-medium secondary study, certain countries, IB English 5, and other listed education routes can waive testing. Duolingo is not listed as an accepted undergraduate test.

Applicants use Common Application, self-report their academic record, pay the application fee or receive an application-based waiver, provide English evidence when required, and complete financial certification after admission. The university does not publish a current international admit rate.

sources.label: Official college page

applicationPlansAndDeadlines.note: The current Fall 2027 application opens August 1, 2026. Nonbinding Early Action I is due November 1 with a decision by January 31; nonbinding Early Action II is due December 1 with a decision by February 15; Regular Decision is due January 1 with a decision by March 31. Completed applications by any of these dates receive full scholarship and Honors consideration.

sources.label: Official college page

applicationRequirements.note: A complete freshman application consists of Common Application, a $55 fee or automatic fee waiver, and self-reported courses and grades. The university does not require an admission essay, recommendation, official transcript, or SAT/ACT score at application. Final records and any scores used in review are verified after enrollment.

sources.label: Official college page

testingPolicy.note: Freshman applicants through Fall 2027 are not required to submit SAT or ACT. Applicants receive full consideration for admission, scholarships, and Honors with or without a score; submitted scores may be self-reported and are verified after enrollment.

sources.label: Official college page

englishProficiency.note: For applications beginning Spring 2027, published minimums are TOEFL iBT 4.5 overall and writing, IELTS 6.5 overall and writing, PTE 59 overall and writing, Cambridge C1 Advanced 180 overall and writing, or Duolingo 120 overall and writing. Country, A-level or IB English, U.S. coursework, SAT, and ACT waiver routes are published; some programs may admit lower scores with an English-support requirement.

sources.label: Official college page

internationalAid.note: UNO offers limited admission-based awards for first-time international students but does not publish a commitment to meet international financial need. Applicants must document the remaining estimated cost for Form I-20; FAFSA-based aid is not an international funding route.

sources.label: Official college page

scholarships.note: The International Tuition Award provides up to $2,000 per year, renewable for a four-year value up to $8,000, for a 3.0 unweighted GPA. The International Book Award provides up to $1,000 for one year for a 2.5 GPA. Both list December 15 as the priority date and do not require FAFSA.

sources.label: Official college page

internationalAdmission.note: International freshmen submit UNO's application, a NACES course-by-course secondary credential evaluation, required math and English evidence, and financial-support documents. UNO requires at least a 2.5 core GPA and does not publish a current international admit rate.

sources.label: Official college page

applicationPlansAndDeadlines.note: The current international page lists November 1 for spring, April 1 for summer, and June 1 for fall as priority dates for immigration processing. Fall 2027 is not explicitly labeled, so June 1 is a planning reference. Scholarship consideration uses an earlier December 15 priority date, and the checklist says applicants should be admitted by January 15.

sources.label: Official college page

applicationRequirements.note: Applicants submit the online application, all secondary transcripts with official English translations, a NACES evaluation, required test or course evidence for English and math, financial-support documents, passport copy, and immunization form. The international undergraduate fee is $30 from Spring 2027.

sources.label: Official college page

testingPolicy.note: UNO's general freshman route can admit applicants with a qualifying core GPA without SAT or ACT, followed by placement testing. International freshmen still need an approved math route—ACT Math 19, SAT Math 510, or qualifying college math—and an English route, so applicants should not treat the international process as fully test-optional.

sources.label: Official college page

englishProficiency.note: International undergraduate minimums are TOEFL iBT 79, IELTS 6.5, Duolingo 100, ACT English 18, or SAT EBRW 500. Qualifying English-country citizenship or U.S. high-school or college study can waive testing, and applicants below the standard can be considered for conditional admission through the Intensive English Language Program.

internationalAid.note: The current international admission page does not publish a need-based aid policy or promise to meet full international need. International students complete proof-of-funding steps after academic materials are reviewed.

sources.label: Official college page

scholarships.note: For 2026–27, general first-year merit awards range from $4,500 to $8,500 per year based on unweighted GPA, with automatic consideration at admission. The official page does not explicitly confirm international eligibility or Fall 2027 amounts, so international applicants should verify before relying on the grid.

sources.label: Official college page

internationalAdmission.note: International applicants apply free, submit secondary and any college transcripts, meet a 2.8 U.S.-equivalent GPA expectation, demonstrate English, and complete the application addendum and proof of funding after initial review. USF does not publish a current international admit rate.

sources.label: Official college page

applicationPlansAndDeadlines.note: USF's current international page does not publish Fall 2027 ED, EA, RD, priority, rolling, document, or notification dates. Applicants should confirm the latest date for admission and Form I-20 processing.

sources.label: Official college page

applicationRequirements.note: There is no application fee. Applicants submit the online application, high-school and any college transcripts, approved English evidence, and—after initial review—the international addendum and proof of funding. Official records and score reports are required before Form I-20.

sources.label: Official college page

testingPolicy.note: The international checklist accepts ACT or SAT section results as English evidence but does not publish a separate Fall 2027 SAT/ACT admission policy. Applicants can meet English through TOEFL, IELTS, Duolingo, English-medium study or U.S. coursework.

sources.label: Official college page

englishProficiency.note: Published minimums are TOEFL iBT 75, IELTS 6.0, or Duolingo 110. An ACT subscore, SAT EBRW result, one year at a U.S. high school, or qualifying U.S. college coursework can also satisfy the requirement, though the current page does not state ACT or SAT numeric thresholds.

scholarships.note: Applicants with complete files by December 1 are automatically considered for the Academic Excellence Scholarship; award criteria and amounts vary by entering class, and any AES level qualifies a nonresident or international recipient for in-state tuition charges. internationalAid.note: Wichita State offers limited merit scholarships but does not publish an international need-aid or full-cost commitment. Every international applicant submits a Certification of Financial Support and recent acceptable bank evidence covering the remaining cost.

sources.label: Official college page

scholarships.note: The latest international viewbook lists a renewable Global Select Scholarship of $5,100 per year for undergraduates with a 3.3-equivalent GPA, but it is not guaranteed and Fall 2027 terms are not yet published. sources.label: Official college page

internationalAdmission.note: International freshmen can qualify on high-school grades without SAT or ACT. sources.label: Official college page

applicationPlansAndDeadlines.note: For Fall 2027, Wichita State offers rolling international processing with three service deadlines: April 15, 2027 for the $75 basic service, June 1 for the $150 standard service, and July 1 for the $250 premium service. sources.label: Official college page

sources.label: Official college page

sources.label: Official college page

englishProficiency.note: Full undergraduate English routes include TOEFL iBT 72 on the former scale or 4.0 on the new scale, IELTS 6.0, Duolingo 105, PTE 49, SAT EBRW 410, ACT English 20, Cambridge AS/A Level English grade C, WSU English exam 80, ELS 112, or completion of Wichita State's highest intensive-English level. Lower published scores allow combined English and academic study.
